title: Code cleanup
body:
This PR implements a couple of changes (to list the most important ones):
- Add capability to detect and react on load/store errors
- Add missing `default` in `unique case`, progagate `'X' in FSM states
- Replace non-unique `case` constructs by `unique case` -> resolves #43 
- Remove unnessary `{}` to avoid linting errors
- Update doc to add `data_err_i` and LSU exceptions -> resolves #44 

The changes are tested in simulation using Verilator. The FPGA bitstream build is completing without errors.

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message: Add capability to detect and react on load/store errors

Add missing `default` in `unique case`, propagate `'X` in FSM states

This commit adds a `default` to all `unique case` statements. Also, in case
FSMs reach an undefined state, the `'X` is propagated to ease detection
in simulation. Both these changes are required by our coding guidelines.

Replace non-unique `case` constructs by `unique case`

Our coding guidelines require the usage of `unique case` constructs with
proper `default` cases. This commit implements this change and also makes sure
that potential `'X` are propagated.
Adjust FSM state signal names to guidelines
Remove unnecessary `{}` to avoid linting errors
Update doc to add `data_err_i` and LSU exceptions

resolved_issues.title: Replace non-unique `case` constructs by `unique case`
resolved_issues.body: There are still many non-unique `case` constructs in the ibex code base that should be replaced by `unique case` constructs with a proper `default` as required by our coding guidelines.

resolved_issues.title: Missing description of input signal from documentation.
resolved_issues.body:
Hi,
Description of input "data_err_i" of the data memory interface is missing from documentation. This signal is currently used only for an assertion. Since it is a top level input, I believe it would be better for the user to read about it in the documentation instead of figuring it out from the RTL.

Best,
Ioannis

problem_statement: Ibex's load-store unit (LSU) does not correctly report data-side error responses as load or store faults. On the data memory interface, `data_rvalid_i` marks the response cycle and `data_err_i` marks that the response failed. When an outstanding data access receives a response with both signals asserted, the LSU currently does not raise the correct load-specific or store-specific error indication for that transaction. The expected behavior is concrete: on an errored response, a failed load must assert `load_err_o` while keeping `store_err_o` low, and a failed store must assert `store_err_o` while keeping `load_err_o` low. This affects LSU handling of data memory interface responses and is triggered whenever a previously accepted load or store request completes with `data_rvalid_i` and `data_err_i` asserted.

title: Compressed hints

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
Fix decoding of C.ADD and C.EBREAK

The RV32C Specification, p106 (RISC-V Unprivileged ISA
V20190305-Base-Ratification) states:

C.ADD adds the values in registers rd and rs2 and writes the result to
register rd. C.ADD expands into add rd, rd, rs2. C.ADD is only valid
when rs2̸=x0; the code points with rs2=x0 correspond to the C.JALR and
C.EBREAK instructions. The code points with rs2̸=x0 and rd=x0 are HINTs.

This essentially says: rs2 == x0 takes precedence when decoding, that's
instr[6:2]. The current code was written with the assumption of
instr[11:7] taking precedence, thus incorrectly decoding a C.ADD HINT.

Fixes lowrisc/ibex#64

Fix handling of C.MV and C.JR

- Decoding must give precedence to rs2 (i.e. instr_i[6:2]) to
  switch between C.MV and C.JR.
  "C.MV is only valid when rs2̸=x0; the code points with rs2=x0
   correspond to the C.JR instruction. The code points with rs2̸=x0
   and rd=x0 are HINTs."

- C.JR is only valid with rs1==x0. Throw an illegal instruction
  exception if that's not the case.
  "C.JR is only valid when rs1̸=x0; the code point with rs1=x0
   is reserved." RV32 Spec, p103

All spec references based on RISC-V Unprivileged ISA
V20190305-Base-Ratification

resolved_issues.title: Evaluate the feasibility of parameterising ibex by XLEN
resolved_issues.body: It could be interesting to support RV64I as well as RV32I (imagine small helper cores, with access to the same address space as a larger 64-bit application cores). Before leaping into doing this, someone needs to do the ground work to see how disruptive it might be, so we can evaluate the potential maintenance / readability costs vs the benefits of supporting an RV64I configuration.

resolved_issues.title: Decode HINT as NOP
resolved_issues.body:
The core fetched an compressed instruction like below.

From a downstream bug report:

core   0: 0xffffffff8000f2ec (0x00009056) add     zero, zero, s5

0x9056 is correctly decoded as HINT instruction by spike, but ibex decode it as illegal C.EBREAK instruction:

https://github.com/lowRISC/stwg-base/blob/master/hw/vendor/lowrisc_ibex/rtl/ibex_compressed_decoder.sv#L215

```
              if (instr_i[11:7] == 5'b0) begin
                // c.ebreak -> ebreak
                instr_o = {32'h00_10_00_73};
                if (instr_i[6:2] != 5'b0) illegal_instr_o = 1'b1;
```

This code first checks if instr[11:7] is zero to determine if it's c.ebreak instruction, then check instr[6:2] to see if it's illegal. However, when instr[6:2] == 0 and instr_i[11:7] != 0, it should be treated as HINT instruction rather than illegal instruction.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_compressed_decoder.sv b/rtl/ibex_compressed_decoder.sv
index 1fac9d559f..d0b31dd7a0 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_compressed_decoder.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_compressed_decoder.sv
@@ -206,24 +206,28 @@ module ibex_compressed_decoder (
 
           3'b100: begin
             if (instr_i[12] == 1'b0) begin
-              // c.mv -> add rd/rs1, x0, rs2
-              instr_o = {7'b0, instr_i[6:2], 5'b0, 3'b0, instr_i[11:7], {OPCODE_OP}};
-
-              if (instr_i[6:2] == 5'b0) begin
+              if (instr_i[6:2] != 5'b0) begin
+                // c.mv -> add rd/rs1, x0, rs2
+                // (c.mv hints are translated into an add hint)
+                instr_o = {7'b0, instr_i[6:2], 5'b0, 3'b0, instr_i[11:7], {OPCODE_OP}};
+              end else begin
                 // c.jr -> jalr x0, rd/rs1, 0
                 instr_o = {12'b0, instr_i[11:7], 3'b0, 5'b0, {OPCODE_JALR}};
+                if (instr_i[11:7] == 5'b0)  illegal_instr_o = 1'b1;
               end
             end else begin
-              // c.add -> add rd, rd, rs2
-              instr_o = {7'b0, instr_i[6:2], instr_i[11:7], 3'b0, instr_i[11:7], {OPCODE_OP}};
-
-              if (instr_i[11:7] == 5'b0) begin
-                // c.ebreak -> ebreak
-                instr_o = {32'h00_10_00_73};
-                if (instr_i[6:2] != 5'b0) illegal_instr_o = 1'b1;
-              end else if (instr_i[6:2] == 5'b0) begin
-                // c.jalr -> jalr x1, rs1, 0
-                instr_o = {12'b0, instr_i[11:7], 3'b000, 5'b00001, {OPCODE_JALR}};
+              if (instr_i[6:2] != 5'b0) begin
+                // c.add -> add rd, rd, rs2
+                // (c.add hints are translated into an add hint)
+                instr_o = {7'b0, instr_i[6:2], instr_i[11:7], 3'b0, instr_i[11:7], {OPCODE_OP}};
+              end else begin
+                if (instr_i[11:7] == 5'b0) begin
+                  // c.ebreak -> ebreak
+                  instr_o = {32'h00_10_00_73};
+                end else begin
+                  // c.jalr -> jalr x1, rs1, 0
+                  instr_o = {12'b0, instr_i[11:7], 3'b000, 5'b00001, {OPCODE_JALR}};
+                end
               end
             end
           end

problem_statement: The Ibex compressed instruction decoder mishandles a RISC-V compressed (RVC) HINT encoding. When the core decodes the 16-bit instruction `0x9056`, which is a legal compressed HINT that corresponds to `add x0, x0, s5`, it currently reports the instruction as an illegal `C.EBREAK` instead. The affected functionality is compressed-instruction decoding in the Ibex core. The bug is triggered by a compressed `C.ADD`-family HINT encoding in which the destination register field is `x0` while the second source register field is non-zero, as in `0x9056`. In that case, the decoder must treat the instruction as a valid compressed HINT, expand it to the corresponding 32-bit `add x0, x0, s5` form, mark it as compressed, and must not raise an illegal-instruction exception.

problem_statement: In the compressed instruction decoder, several RISC-V compressed HINT encodings are being reported as illegal instructions. In the RISC-V C extension, these encodings are legal HINT/no-op forms: `C.LI` with destination register `x0`, `C.LUI` with destination register `x0` and a non-zero immediate (for example `0x7065`), and `C.SRLI`, `C.SRAI`, or `C.SLLI` with shift amount `0`. Ibex currently treats these compressed instructions as illegal instead of recognizing them as valid compressed HINTs. The bug affects `ibex_compressed_decoder` whenever one of those specific HINT forms is presented. The expected behavior is that these instructions are still recognized as compressed instructions and do not raise the illegal-instruction indication.

title: Fix perf counters
body:
This PR solves two problems in the performance counters:
1. Fix increment of performance counters
2. Make sure performance counters are not accidentally optimized away during synthesis. Only those are optimized away, which are disabled.

It resolves #80.

The changes have been tested using Verilator and Vivado.

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
Fix performance counters

Without this commit, the performance counters mhpmcounter3(h)-
mhpmcounter31(h) are optimized away during synthesis due to
`X`-values in the address decoder masks. This commit replaces
these masks with offsets and instead masks the input address
before comparison.

To enable the synthesizer optimizing away unused counters,
the masks for these counters are set to zero.

Correct performance counter increment

Prior to this commit, the next counter value was not based on the
current value.

resolved_issues.title: Number of performance counters
resolved_issues.body:
the parameter MHPMCounterNum does not seem to influence the number of performance counters. I synthesized the core once with MHPMCounterNum=1 and then with MHPMCounterNum=8 and it results in almost exactly the same area.

by looking at the code I also don't see how this parameter is changing the number of physically present counters/flipflops. I'm pretty sure there are 32 64b registers and 32 64b adders no matter what the parameters are.

I think MHPMCounterWidth has the same problem. it probably only counts to the desired width, but the registers [63:MHPMCounteWidth] cannot be optimized away.

the problem with the width can be easily fixed by changing:
```
csr_rdata_int = mhpmcounter_q[mhpmcounter_idx][63:32];
```
to
```
csr_rdata_int[MHPMCounterWidth-1:0] = mhpmcounter_q[mhpmcounter_idx][MHPMCounterWidth-1:32];
csr_rdata_int[32-1:MHPMCounterWidth-32] = '0;
```

if mhpmcounter_q[63:MHPMCounterWidth] is never accessed, the synthesizer can optimize it away. otherwise these registers are there but cannot really be used.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv b/rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv
index 8110531d03..3bd6d29f55 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv
@@ -186,10 +186,8 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
   /////////////
 
   logic [$bits(csr_num_e)-1:0] csr_addr;
-  logic [4:0]                  unused_csr_addr;
   assign csr_addr           = {csr_addr_i};
   assign mhpmcounter_idx    = csr_addr[4:0];
-  assign unused_csr_addr    = csr_addr[9:5];
 
   assign illegal_csr_priv   = 1'b0; // we only support M-mode
   assign illegal_csr_write  = (csr_addr[11:10] == 2'b11) && csr_we_int;
@@ -242,7 +240,7 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
       CSR_MINSTRETH:     csr_rdata_int = mhpmcounter_q[2][63:32];
 
       default: begin
-        if (csr_addr_i == CSR_MCOUNTER_SETUP_MASK) begin
+        if ((csr_addr & CSR_MASK_MCOUNTER) == CSR_OFF_MCOUNTER_SETUP) begin
           csr_rdata_int = mhpmevent[mhpmcounter_idx];
           // check access to non-existent or already covered CSRs
           if ((csr_addr[4:0] == 5'b00000) ||     // CSR_MCOUNTINHIBIT
@@ -251,7 +249,7 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
             illegal_csr = csr_access_i;
           end
 
-        end else if (csr_addr_i == CSR_MCOUNTER_MASK) begin
+        end else if ((csr_addr & CSR_MASK_MCOUNTER) == CSR_OFF_MCOUNTER) begin
           csr_rdata_int = mhpmcounter_q[mhpmcounter_idx][31: 0];
           // check access to non-existent or already covered CSRs
           if ((csr_addr[4:0] == 5'b00000) ||     // CSR_MCYCLE
@@ -260,7 +258,7 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
             illegal_csr = csr_access_i;
           end
 
-        end else if (csr_addr_i == CSR_MCOUNTERH_MASK) begin
+        end else if ((csr_addr & CSR_MASK_MCOUNTER) == CSR_OFF_MCOUNTERH) begin
           csr_rdata_int = mhpmcounter_q[mhpmcounter_idx][63:32];
           // check access to non-existent or already covered CSRs
           if ((csr_addr[4:0] == 5'b00000) ||     // CSR_MCYCLEH
@@ -378,9 +376,9 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
       default: begin
         if (csr_we_int == 1'b1) begin
           // performance counters and event selector
-          if (csr_addr_i == CSR_MCOUNTER_MASK) begin
+          if ((csr_addr & CSR_MASK_MCOUNTER) == CSR_OFF_MCOUNTER) begin
             mhpmcounter_we[mhpmcounter_idx] = 1'b1;
-          end else if (csr_addr_i == CSR_MCOUNTERH_MASK) begin
+          end else if ((csr_addr & CSR_MASK_MCOUNTER) == CSR_OFF_MCOUNTERH) begin
             mhpmcounterh_we[mhpmcounter_idx] = 1'b1;
           end
         end
@@ -515,22 +513,27 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
   assign mcountinhibit       = mcountinhibit_q | mcountinhibit_force;
 
   // event selection (hardwired) & control
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[0]  = 1'b1;                // mcycle
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[1]  = 1'b0;                // reserved
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[2]  = insn_ret_i;          // minstret
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[3]  = lsu_busy_i;          // cycles waiting for data memory
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[4]  = imiss_i & ~pc_set_i; // cycles waiting for instr fetches ex.
-                                                     // jumps and branches
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[5]  = mem_load_i;          // num of loads
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[6]  = mem_store_i;         // num of stores
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[7]  = jump_i;              // num of jumps (unconditional)
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[8]  = branch_i;            // num of branches (conditional)
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[9]  = branch_taken_i;      // num of taken branches (conditional)
-  assign mhpmcounter_incr[10] = is_compressed_i      // num of compressed instr
-      & id_valid_i & is_decoding_i;
-
-  for (genvar i=3+MHPMCounterNum; i<32; i++) begin : gen_mhpmcounter_incr_inactive
-    assign mhpmcounter_incr[i] = 1'b0;
+  always_comb begin : gen_mhpmcounter_incr
+
+    // active counters
+    mhpmcounter_incr[0]  = 1'b1;                // mcycle
+    mhpmcounter_incr[1]  = 1'b0;                // reserved
+    mhpmcounter_incr[2]  = insn_ret_i;          // minstret
+    mhpmcounter_incr[3]  = lsu_busy_i;          // cycles waiting for data memory
+    mhpmcounter_incr[4]  = imiss_i & ~pc_set_i; // cycles waiting for instr fetches ex.
+                                                // jumps and branches
+    mhpmcounter_incr[5]  = mem_load_i;          // num of loads
+    mhpmcounter_incr[6]  = mem_store_i;         // num of stores
+    mhpmcounter_incr[7]  = jump_i;              // num of jumps (unconditional)
+    mhpmcounter_incr[8]  = branch_i;            // num of branches (conditional)
+    mhpmcounter_incr[9]  = branch_taken_i;      // num of taken branches (conditional)
+    mhpmcounter_incr[10] = is_compressed_i      // num of compressed instr
+        & id_valid_i & is_decoding_i;
+
+    // inactive counters
+    for (int unsigned i=3+MHPMCounterNum; i<32; i++) begin : gen_mhpmcounter_incr_inactive
+      mhpmcounter_incr[i] = 1'b0;
+    end
   end
 
   // event selector (hardwired, 0 means no event)
@@ -538,6 +541,7 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
 
     // activate all
     for (int i=0; i<32; i++) begin : gen_mhpmevent_active
+      mhpmevent[i]    =   '0;
       mhpmevent[i][i] = 1'b1;
     end
 
@@ -556,10 +560,15 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
       mhpmcounter_mask[i] = {64{1'b1}};
     end
 
-    for (int i=3; i<32; i++) begin : gen_mask_configurable
+    for (int unsigned i=3; i<3+MHPMCounterNum; i++) begin : gen_mask_configurable
       // mhpmcounters have a configurable width
       mhpmcounter_mask[i] = {{64-MHPMCounterWidth{1'b0}}, {MHPMCounterWidth{1'b1}}};
     end
+
+    for (int unsigned i=3+MHPMCounterNum; i<32; i++) begin : gen_mask_inactive
+      // mask inactive mhpmcounters
+      mhpmcounter_mask[i] = '0;
+    end
   end
 
   // update
@@ -570,7 +579,7 @@ module ibex_cs_registers #(
 
       // increment
       if (mhpmcounter_incr[i] & ~mcountinhibit[i]) begin
-        mhpmcounter_n[i] = mhpmcounter_mask[i] & (mhpmcounter_n[i] + 64'h1);
+        mhpmcounter_n[i] = mhpmcounter_mask[i] & (mhpmcounter_q[i] + 64'h1);
       end
 
       // write
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_defines.sv b/rtl/ibex_defines.sv
index bcc8c4c5b7..ec4943c290 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_defines.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_defines.sv
@@ -240,15 +240,17 @@ typedef enum logic[11:0] {
   CSR_DSCRATCH1 = 12'h7b3, // optional
 
   // Machine Counter/Timers
-  CSR_MCOUNTINHIBIT       = 12'h320,
-  CSR_MCYCLE              = 12'hB00,
-  CSR_MCYCLEH             = 12'hB80,
-  CSR_MINSTRET            = 12'hB02,
-  CSR_MINSTRETH           = 12'hB82,
-
-  CSR_MCOUNTER_SETUP_MASK = 12'b0011_001X_XXXX, // actually 12'h323 - 12'h33F
-  CSR_MCOUNTER_MASK       = 12'b1011_000X_XXXX, // actually 12'hB03 - 12'hB1F
-  CSR_MCOUNTERH_MASK      = 12'b1011_100X_XXXX  // actually 12'hB83 - 12'hB9F
+  CSR_MCOUNTINHIBIT      = 12'h320,
+  CSR_MCYCLE             = 12'hB00,
+  CSR_MCYCLEH            = 12'hB80,
+  CSR_MINSTRET           = 12'hB02,
+  CSR_MINSTRETH          = 12'hB82
 } csr_num_e;
 
+// CSR mhpmcounter-related offsets and mask
+parameter logic [11:0] CSR_OFF_MCOUNTER_SETUP = 12'h320; // mcounter_setup @ 12'h323 - 12'h33F
+parameter logic [11:0] CSR_OFF_MCOUNTER       = 12'hB00; // mcounter       @ 12'hB03 - 12'hB1F
+parameter logic [11:0] CSR_OFF_MCOUNTERH      = 12'hB80; // mcounterh      @ 12'hB83 - 12'hB9F
+parameter logic [11:0] CSR_MASK_MCOUNTER      = 12'hFE0;
+
 endpackage
prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout the baseline that matches fix.patch.
cd /home/ibex
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 826da1522f424036a5170bf46fd4997f0156339d
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install toolchains (default flow with fallback).
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

install_ok=0
if [[ -f ci/install-build-deps.sh ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing toolchains via ci/install-build-deps.sh"

  if [[ -f ci/vars.env ]]; then
    echo "[INFO] Loading tool versions from ci/vars.env"
    set -a
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source ci/vars.env
    set +a
  elif [[ -f ci/vars.yml || -f ci/vars.yaml ]]; then
    echo "[INFO] Loading tool versions from ci/vars.yml"
    /usr/bin/python3 - <<'PY' > /tmp/ibex_vars.sh
import os
import shlex
import yaml

path = "ci/vars.yml"
if not os.path.exists(path):
    path = "ci/vars.yaml"

with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}

if not isinstance(data, dict):
    raise SystemExit(f"Unexpected YAML structure in {path}: {type(data).__name__}")

vars_dict = data
if isinstance(data.get("variables"), dict):
    vars_dict = data["variables"]

for key, value in vars_dict.items():
    if isinstance(value, (str, int, float)) and key.isidentifier():
        print(f"export {key}={shlex.quote(str(value))}")
PY
    set -a
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source /tmp/ibex_vars.sh
    set +a
  else
    echo "[WARN] No ci/vars.env or ci/vars.yml found; running install script without explicit version vars"
  fi

  chmod +x ci/install-build-deps.sh
  set +e
  bash ci/install-build-deps.sh
  rc=$?
  set -e
  if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
    install_ok=1
  else
    echo "[WARN] ci/install-build-deps.sh failed (rc=$rc) on this OS; will try fallback installer"
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] ci/install-build-deps.sh not found at 826da1522f424036a5170bf46fd4997f0156339d; will use fallback installer"
fi

if [[ $install_ok -ne 1 ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Fallback toolchain install: minimal deps for Verilator + fusesoc flows"
  apt-get update
  apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends pkg-config
  rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

  if [[ -n "${VERILATOR_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    echo "[INFO] Installing Verilator ${VERILATOR_VERSION} (prebuilt)"
    mkdir -p /tools/verilator
    verilator_tag="${VERILATOR_VERSION:-v4.210}"
    if [[ "$verilator_tag" != v* ]]; then
      verilator_tag="v${verilator_tag}"
    fi
    min_verilator_tag="v4.210"
    if [[ "$(printf '%s\n' "${verilator_tag#v}" "${min_verilator_tag#v}" | sort -V | tail -n1)" == "${min_verilator_tag#v}" ]]; then
      verilator_tag="${min_verilator_tag}"
    fi
    curl -fLs -o /tmp/verilator.tar.gz \
      "https://storage.googleapis.com/verilator-builds/verilator-${verilator_tag}.tar.gz"
    tar -C /tools/verilator -xzf /tmp/verilator.tar.gz
    ln -sfn "/tools/verilator/${verilator_tag}" /tools/verilator/current
    if [[ -n "${VERILATOR_VERSION:-}" && "$verilator_tag" != "${VERILATOR_VERSION}" ]]; then
      ln -sfn "/tools/verilator/${verilator_tag}" "/tools/verilator/${VERILATOR_VERSION}"
    fi
    verilated_cpp="/tools/verilator/${verilator_tag}/share/verilator/include/verilated.cpp"
    if [[ -f "$verilated_cpp" ]] && ! grep -q '^#include <limits>$' "$verilated_cpp"; then
      echo "[INFO] Patching verilator include for Ubuntu 22.04 compatibility: $verilated_cpp"
      sed -i '/^#include <sstream>$/a #include <limits>' "$verilated_cpp"
    fi
  else
    echo "[INFO] Installing Verilator via apt (no VERILATOR_VERSION set)"
    apt-get update
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends verilator
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  fi

  python -m pip install -U pip
  if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
    echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt (filtered)"
    grep -v -E '^\s*-r\s+vendor/google_riscv-dv/requirements\.txt\s*$' \
      python-requirements.txt > /tmp/ibex_python_requirements.txt
    python -m pip install -r /tmp/ibex_python_requirements.txt
  else
    python -m pip install -U fusesoc edalize mako
  fi

  mkdir -p /tools/riscv
  curl -Ls -o /tmp/rv32-toolchain.tar.xz \
    https://github.com/lowRISC/lowrisc-toolchains/releases/download/20220210-1/lowrisc-toolchain-gcc-rv32imcb-20220210-1.tar.xz
  tar -C /tools/riscv -xf /tmp/rv32-toolchain.tar.xz --strip-components=1
fi

# Stage 3: persist /tools PATH (verilator/riscv/verible, etc.)
if [[ -n "${VERILATOR_VERSION:-}" && -d "/tools/verilator/${VERILATOR_VERSION}/bin" ]]; then
  ln -sfn "/tools/verilator/${VERILATOR_VERSION}" /tools/verilator/current
fi

cat > /etc/ibex_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv-isa-sim/bin /tools/verilator/current/bin /tools/verible/bin /tools/riscv/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

  echo "source /etc/ibex_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/ibex_bash_env
fi

# Stage 4: apply PATH for current shell
source /etc/ibex_tools_path.sh
problem_statement: In the Ibex Control and Status Register (CSR) logic, optional machine performance counter CSRs are not decoded correctly. On this 32-bit core, software accesses to counters beyond the mandatory `mcycle` and `minstret` counters, such as `mhpmcounter3`, are not handled as valid CSR accesses: a write to `mhpmcounter3` does not reliably take effect, and a subsequent read of the same CSR can return the wrong value or raise an illegal CSR indication. The expected behavior is that implemented optional performance counter CSRs `mhpmcounter3` through `mhpmcounter31` decode like normal machine CSRs; for example, a 32-bit write to `mhpmcounter3` followed by a read of `mhpmcounter3` should return the written low 32-bit value without flagging the access as illegal. This affects the performance-counter CSR decode path and is triggered when software reads or writes optional performance counter CSRs beyond `mcycle` and `minstret`.

title: Spec compliant trap handling
body:
This PR mainly modifies the trap handling infrastructure to comply with the RISC-V privileged spec, draft versions 1.11. To this end, additional CSRs were added.

All exceptions now jump to the base address of the trap-vector table. Interrupts are handled in vectored mode and jump to the base address + 4*irq_id. The exception cause is stored in `mcause` and `mtval` has been added to hold additional information (illegal instruction for illegal instruction exception, address of faulting transaction part for LSU errors).

To implement these changes the AGU mux for misaligned loads/stores has been reworked.
In addition, the `mscratch` CSR has been implemented.

This PR resolves: #97 and #70.

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message: Order CSR assignments according to their address

Rework AGU mux for misaligned loads/stores

This operation only depends on the LSU detecting a misaligned address.
Previously, the mux control was scattered across ID stage, controller
and decoder. With this commit, all the relevant code for this operation
is moved into the ID stage and also streamlined.

Add `mtval` CSR

`mtval` can provide additional information to trap handlers.
In case of load/store errors, it holds the failing address.
For illegal instruction exceptions, it holds the illegal instruction.
Reduce width of `mcause` CSR

Make `mtvec` CSR compliant to spec

The LSBs indicate the vector mode. They are set to vectored for Ibex.

Switch to RISC-V spec compliant trap handling

For exceptions, the Ibex always jumps to the trap vector base address
specified in `mtvec`. The exception cause is specified in `mcause` with
possibly additional information in `mtval`.

Interrupts are handled in vectored mode as before.
Mask LSB of `mepc` CSR to 0 for writes initiated by software
Add `mscratch` CSR
Doc: use ``csr_num``.FIELD_NAME syntax when discussing CSR fields

Doc: remove draft when mentioning RISC-V Priv Spec v.1.11

This version of the spec has been ratified in the meantime.

resolved_issues.body:
Hi guys (@vogelpi , @imphil )

according to the Priv ISA Spec of RISC-V 1.10, you should handle the exceptions by always jumping to mtvec rather than vectoring them as it was in the past

Look at the section
3.1.12 Machine Trap-Vector Base-Address Register (mtvec)
of this document please: https://riscv.org/specifications/privileged-isa/

I have already done it in RISCY.
So now in the controller everytime you get an exception you set exc_pc_mux_o to exceptions:
https://github.com/pulp-platform/riscv/blob/master/rtl/riscv_controller.sv#L731

and in the IF stage you always jump to the same address regardless the exception cause:
https://github.com/pulp-platform/riscv/blob/master/rtl/riscv_if_stage.sv#L141

 Exceptions and Interrupts
 =========================
 
-Ibex currently implements a free-form vectored trap handler mechanism for interrupts and exceptions.
-The base address of the interrupt vector table is given by the boot address (must be aligned to 256 bytes, i.e., its least significant byte must be 0x00).
+Ibex implements trap handling for interrupts and exceptions according to the RISC-V Privileged Specification, version 1.11.
+
+All exceptions cause the core to jump to the base address of the vector table in the ``mtvec`` CSR.
+Interrupts are handled in vectored mode, i.e., the core jumps to the base address plus four times the interrupt cause number.
+
+The base address of the vector table is given by the boot address (must be aligned to 256 bytes, i.e., its least significant byte must be 0x00).
 The most significant 3 bytes of the boot address given to the core are used for the first instruction fetch of the core and as the basis of the interrupt vector table.
 The core starts fetching at the address made by concatenating the most significant 3 bytes of the boot address and the reset value (0x80) as the least significant byte.
 The boot address can be changed after the first instruction was fetched to change the interrupt vector table address.
 It is assumed that the boot address is supplied via a register to avoid long paths to the instruction fetch unit.
-The table below lists the supported interrupts and exceptions and the corresponding address offset in the interrupt vector table.
-
-+------------+-----------------------------+
-| Address    | Description                 |

-| **0x7C**   |                             |
-+------------+-----------------------------+
-| **0x80**   | Reset                       |
-+------------+-----------------------------+
-| **0x84**   | Illegal Instruction         |
-+------------+-----------------------------+
-| **0x88**   | ECALL Instruction Executed  |

problem_statement:
Ibex's machine-mode trap control and status register (CSR) interface is incomplete relative to the RISC-V privileged specification. In the buggy baseline, the standard `mscratch` CSR is missing, the architectural `mtvec` value is not exposed as a normal machine trap-vector register that software can read back, and the full exception state is not available through the standard trap CSRs because there is no `mtval` register for the trap-specific value.

Ibex should expose the standard machine trap CSR set needed for spec-compliant trap handling: `mtvec` must read back the configured trap-vector value, `mscratch` must behave as a normal read/write scratch CSR, and when an exception is recorded the trap state visible to software must include the saved exception PC in `mepc`, the trap cause in `mcause`, and the trap-specific value in `mtval`. This affects the trap-handling CSR logic whenever software accesses machine trap CSRs or the core saves exception state for a trap handler.

title: Fix LSU + lint errors
body:
I prepared this PR to get urgent stuff fixed before the bigger changes for the controller and interrupts/exceptions.

This PR contains two commits:
- The first one is a cleanup of the LSU that also fixes a critical error. Previously, misaligned loads/stores were broken as the byte enable generation and read data alignment for the second transaction part were not working. - The second one fixes recently introduced linting errors.

problem_statement: Ibex mishandles misaligned 32-bit stores in the load-store unit. When a store address is not 32-bit aligned and the access must be split across two adjacent 32-bit words, the address and byte-enable calculation for the second memory transaction is incorrect, so the split store does not preserve the original byte lanes. In the failing boundary case, a 32-bit store to an address whose two least significant bits are `01` is not performed as the required pair of aligned writes. The correct behavior is to issue two aligned store transactions that together write the same four bytes as the original store: the first transaction writes byte lanes 1-3 of the lower word, and the second transaction writes byte lane 0 of the next word. This affects the load-store unit and the address generation used for the second part of a misaligned store, and it is triggered by a misaligned 32-bit store that crosses a 32-bit word boundary.

resolved_issues.title: Tracer support for compressed instructions
resolved_issues.body:
The tracer reuses the RVFI signals. `rvfi_insn` holds the current instruction, but for the RISC-V formal verification this needs to be the instruction which is inserted into the core.
For compressed instructions the core will decode those to uncompressed instruction, which are then used internally.

The tracer currently prints `INVALID` for compressed instructions (https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/issues/147#issuecomment-511083710) as it has no support for compressed instructions. 

For the tracer we can either add an additional output signal with the uncompressed instruction or add support in the tracer for decoding compressed instructions.
@imphil do you have an opinion here?

I am running regression with new tracer with RVFI interface, seems to me the generated trace is not as expected.  Looks like the logic used to generate rvfi_valid_int is one cycle off. The decoded instruction is not captured properly.

![Screenshot from 2019-07-11 15-00-11](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34581368/61088279-dd2f8880-a3ec-11e9-9464-f63f728013de.png)

resolved_issues.title: Rework RVFI to align with decoder
resolved_issues.body: As reported in https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/issues/147 the tracer, which is based on the RVFI signals is not working correct. This is because `rvfi_valid` signal depends on the state of the decoder (retired instruction). The current implementation looked for changes in the program counter in order to be only valid if the new program counter is actually used. With https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/pull/150 it should now be possible to change this implementation so that a retired instruction can be marked as valid without waiting for the next instruction.

problem_statement:
The Ibex RISC-V Formal Interface (RVFI) used by the execution tracer is not aligned with instruction retirement. In the current behavior, `rvfi_valid` can become true only after a later program-counter change, so the RVFI record for a retired instruction is emitted one cycle late and may be paired with the PC and instruction data of a different instruction. This affects the RVFI/tracer path that records retired instructions.

Expected behavior is that every retired instruction becomes visible to RVFI immediately when it retires, without waiting for a later PC update, and that each RVFI record corresponds to exactly one retired instruction in retirement order. The instruction value in that record, the PC of the retired instruction, and the next PC or branch target must all describe the same instruction. This must also work for 16-bit RISC-V compressed instructions, including consecutive compressed instructions: they should appear as separate retire records with 2-byte PC advances and a usable instruction value for tracing, rather than being delayed, merged into a later record, or shown as invalid.

problem_statement: When Ibex handles an external debug halt request (`debug_req_i`), it should enter debug mode by jumping to the configured debug halt address (`DmHaltAddr`) and saving the interrupted program counter in the debug PC CSR (`dpc`). The expected behavior is that this request is handled consistently: either the core completes debug entry with `dpc` set to the interrupted PC, or the transient request is ignored and the core stays out of debug mode.

title: Decoder: fix signaling and detection of illegal instructions
body:
This commit fixes two bugs in the decoder:

1. For illegal branch condition selections, the illegal instruction
condition must be signaled as long as the instruction is being executed
and not just during the first cycle, as the controller cannot interrupt
multicycle instructions.

2. Illegal instructions should also be signaled when `instr[28]` is set
for register-register ALU operations. Previously, these were not
signaled as the original design used `instr[28]` to encode custom bit-
manipulation instructions.

These bugs were discovered by @taoliug. This resolves issue #163.

Previously, this signal was only cleared when starting the next
multi-cycle instruction.

This signal should only be evaluated if the ID/EX stage currently

resolved_issues.title: instr_multicycle_done is not asserted, continuous register writes
resolved_issues.body:
While executing the code shown below:
![Screenshot from 2019-08-05 18-14-11](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/62504340-e2de7b00-b7ac-11e9-8b26-0cc4090ccec3.png)
We see this incorrect behavior in the core:
![Screenshot from 2019-08-05 18-13-52](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/62504356-ee31a680-b7ac-11e9-8d28-748683269f7e.png)

As shown, the `addi` instruction at PC `0x80000088` appears to correctly load register `x13` with the value `0xa5a5a5a5`, but at the very next instruction (PC: `0x8000008c`), we can see from the trace log that `x13` now has the value `0xa5a5de17`. 
![Screenshot from 2019-08-05 18-12-33](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/62504456-76b04700-b7ad-11e9-94ab-524900644a48.png)

From the waveform, `rf_reg[13]` is written correctly by the `addi` after adding the immediate value `0x5a5` (`alu_operand_b_i`), and becomes `0xa5a5a5a5`. After this, the testbench does not assert the `instr_gnt_i` for a number of cycles, leading the core to stay in the DECODE phase while waiting for the next instruction fetch. However, we see that `rf_reg[13]` keeps getting written with the incremented values of `alu_result` in every consecutive cycle that the core waits, as `instr_multicycle_done_q` in the ID stage does not go high after the `addi` finishes. This keeps `regfile_we` at 1, causing the continuous writes.

problem_statement: When a single-cycle instruction such as `addi` completes in Ibex and the next instruction fetch is stalled because the instruction-fetch grant signal (`instr_gnt_i`) stays low, the core can remain in the instruction-decode (ID) stage with the register-file write-enable signal (`regfile_we`) still asserted. During those stalled cycles, the destination register of the completed instruction may be written again even though no new instruction has arrived. The affected functionality is the ID-stage logic that determines when the current instruction has finished and whether register-file writes remain enabled while the instruction-fetch interface is stalled. Once the single-cycle instruction has committed its result, `regfile_we` must be deasserted on every cycle while the core waits for the next instruction-fetch grant, and the destination register must retain its committed value throughout that stall.

title: Rework CSR-related pipeline flushes
body:
This commit clarifies why CSR-related pipeline flushes are needed (e.g. when enabling interrupts), only introduces them when doing the critical modifications (write/set bits in `mstatus` and `mie` CSRs
for enabling interrupts, reads and clears are uncritical for these CSRs), and makes sure the controller is actually able to start handling interrupts while doing a CSR-related pipeline flush.

This resolves lowrisc/ibex#6.

problem_statement: When software uses RISC-V Control and Status Register (CSR) instructions to enable interrupts through the `mie` (machine interrupt-enable) and `mstatus` (machine status) CSRs while an interrupt is already pending, Ibex can perform the CSR-related pipeline flush and then resume normal instruction execution instead of entering the interrupt handler. The failing case is a back-to-back sequence that first enables the relevant source in `mie`, then sets the global interrupt-enable bit in `mstatus`, and then immediately clears that bit again: the pending interrupt can be lost and a following non-interrupt instruction can retire. The affected logic is the CSR-related pipeline-flush and interrupt-entry path around updates to `mie` and `mstatus`. Correct behavior is that once those CSR write/set operations make a pending interrupt eligible for service, the core must take the interrupt before normal execution resumes, even if the next instruction would disable interrupts again.

problem_statement: `ibex_load_store_unit` has a data-interface timing bug. The outgoing request signal `data_req_o` is coupled to the current response/error inputs `data_rvalid_i` and `data_err_i`, creating a slave-to-master-to-slave combinational path on the Load-Store Unit (LSU) interface. In the misaligned access path, where one load or store that crosses a word boundary is split into two word-aligned memory transactions, this also changes visible behavior: the second transaction can be held off until the first transaction returns a response. The expected behavior is concrete: once the first part of a misaligned access has been granted, the LSU must be able to issue the second request before the first response arrives, independent of the current values of `data_rvalid_i` and `data_err_i`. If the first response later reports an error after that second request has already been issued, the LSU must report the error for the original access, remain busy until the already-issued second response is received, ignore that abandoned second response for architectural completion, and only then return to idle. The bug is triggered when a misaligned data access has its first transfer granted and the first response returns with `data_err_i` asserted while the LSU still needs to manage the second transfer.

problem_statement: In the instruction-side fetch path, the instruction request output (`instr_req_o`) has a combinational dependency on the instruction return-valid input (`instr_rvalid_i`). When the prefetch buffer already has a granted fetch outstanding and is deciding whether it can issue the next instruction fetch request, a change on `instr_rvalid_i` can immediately change `instr_req_o`, creating a slave-to-master-to-slave timing path on the instruction interface in systems that do not pipeline these signals. The affected functionality is the instruction prefetch buffer / fetch interface. The correct behavior is that `instr_req_o` must not change combinationally in response to `instr_rvalid_i` within the same cycle; receipt of an instruction return-valid may only affect request generation in a later cycle.

problem_statement: Recent instruction-side logic and prefetch-buffer changes broke the instruction fetch handshake in Ibex. The instruction-side prefetch buffer issues fetches through a request/grant/response interface: `instr_req_o` requests an instruction fetch, `instr_gnt_i` accepts that request, and the returned instruction data arrives later. In the failing behavior, if a fetch request is made and the grant does not arrive immediately, the prefetch buffer can stop treating that fetch as pending and can advance to a different address before the original request has been accepted. This can desynchronize instruction fetches and cause execution to stop early in the tracing example. The affected logic is the instruction-side prefetch buffer and its request/address tracking. When a fetch is pending but has not yet been granted, including the sequential fetch immediately after a granted branch fetch, `instr_req_o` must remain asserted and `instr_addr_o` must remain at the same word-aligned address until `instr_gnt_i` acknowledges that request.

resolved_issues.title: Incorrect `mepc` value after irq is taken
resolved_issues.body:
Hi all,
During a test, this segment of code is running on the core:
![Screenshot from 2019-09-16 11-19-14](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/64982799-e406cb80-d873-11e9-8d8e-19d60156213b.png)
At `PC=0x80000276` (a `nop` instruction), our testbench asserts a software interrupt, as shown from the waves below:
![Screenshot from 2019-09-16 11-23-43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/64983038-74dda700-d874-11e9-8709-7f0dfce5636f.png)
However, we see that `mepc_q` gets set to `0x80000274` after this interrupt is detected and handling begins, meaning that after the interrupt handler has ended, the core will jump back to this address, but as you can see from the code snippet, this is a misaligned address, so Ibex immediately takes an illegal instruction exception, and fails the test.  This address comes from the `exception_pc`, which is muxed to the value of `pc_if_i`, which for some reason is set to this misaligned address, and is less than the `pc_id_i`.

resolved_issues.title: Instruction address changes before a request/grant handshake
resolved_issues.body:
The instruction interface of Ibex allows to change the address while asserting request and waiting for a grant. This behavior is inherited from RI5CY. If I remember correctly, the primary reason for having this in RI5CY is that in multi-core configurations (PULP) with a shared instruction cache, it allows to reduce contention on the cache and leads to notable performance gains. This can also be beneficial for performance in Ibex (e.g. in case the core takes a branch while the instruction interface is still waiting for the grant of a previous request) but has over and over again confused people.

There were several GitHub issues where we needed to explain this to users, but the problem was usually something else. However, we never had an issue to discuss if we want to change this behavior or keep it.

I think we should remove it. Ibex is a different core that does not target multi-core configs with shared I-caches, so the actual performance benefit is probably relatively low. Instead, it is confusing and complicates translation into popular protocols such as AXI/AHB (it is however legal for TileLink interconnects) as mentioned in pulp-platform/riscv#128.

WDYT?

resolved_issues.title: Instruction fetch error execution
resolved_issues.body:
Hi all,
![Screenshot from 2019-09-19 16-18-58](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/65288479-d06d9600-dafb-11e9-8060-11e8c25877e0.png)
![Screenshot from 2019-09-19 16-23-24](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/65288484-d2cff000-dafb-11e9-8ed2-266b8f6eac41.png)
Above is a snippet of disassembled code I was running on Ibex, and the associated section in the core tracer. At `PC=0x8000087c`, there should be a `nop` instruction, but Ibex shows execution of `lui x19, 0xabd6c000` at this PC.
![Screenshot from 2019-09-19 16-34-44](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/65288550-10cd1400-dafc-11e9-8a99-2d01a2d3525b.png)
At the location in the waves where the cursor is, the active `instr_grant` and `instr_rvalid` are responding to the `request` corresponding to the address `0x8000087c`. At the same time, the testbench randomly asserts an `instr_error` during the instruction fetch response, and randomizes the returned `instr_rdata`, as the request has returned with an error response. The random data here happens to be the value `0xabd6c9b7`, which Ibex decodes as the same exact `lui` instruction from above.  We should expect that this should not be executed then, since an error was returned to the core, but we can see that at time 4,113,000ns, Ibex raises the register file `we_a_i` write enable signal, and writes the data `0xabd6c000` to register `0x13`, effectively completing execution of this random instruction data even though there was an instruction fetch error associated with this response. Immediately after completing execution of the randomly generated data at `PC=0x8000087c`, the core jumps to the instruction fetch exception handler at `PC=80014000`, and runs the handler code.
This issue only exists for the instruction fetch interface; for similar situations involving load/store errors that the testbench generates, Ibex will not commit load data to the regfile, or write store data to our memory model, and will only run the faulty memory instruction to completion once it has finished executing the associated exception handler code.

  as soon as the first transaction completed. This commits makes

resolved_issues.title: DMEM fault during misaligned memory access
resolved_issues.body:
Hi all,
When running this set of instructions:
![Screenshot from 2019-10-04 16-43-38](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/66245995-26c70100-e6c6-11e9-8347-b284c658e62c.png)
The following waves were generated:
![Screenshot from 2019-10-04 16-47-11](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/66246078-a1901c00-e6c6-11e9-839a-a188fce292f5.png)
The `sw` instructions at `PC=0x800058d0` has a misaligned memory address, and is thus split into two internal memory transactions. In the waves, around 395,800,000ps corresponds to the memory response to the first of these two transactions, which is when the testbench randomly asserts a memory fault here. According to Ibex documentation for this situation, the second memory transaction should continue as normal, ignoring the response data, and then the core needs to also jump to the corresponding fault handler (located at `PC=0x80014000` in our case). The LSU's FSM transitions to it's error handling states from the misaligned transaction states, and the core jumps to `0x80014000` (which encodes the instruction `j 80014080`) directly after `0x800058d0`, but while executing this jump instruction, the core jumps to `0x8001e112` instead, throwing an illegal instruction exception, and then proceeds to wait for the `rvalid` corresponding to the second part of the original misaligned transaction. This occurs around 395,835,000ps, and after this, the core jumps back to the fault handler, and fully executes it. This intermediate PC of `0x8001e112` is calculated as the incorrect jump address from load address data that's already in the execution pipeline, and is muxed through due to `lsu_addr_incr_req_i` going high while waiting for the second half of the misaligned memory transaction to complete. Maybe a potential solution for this would be to only jump to the fault handler after the second part of the misaligned transactions has completed?
Best,
Udi

If the first transaction returns a memory fault, the unit can report the store as complete and raise the store fault immediately, even though the second half of the split access is still outstanding. The expected behavior is that the second transaction is still issued and allowed to finish, and the store fault is reported only after responses for both halves of the split access have been received.

resolved_issues.title: Debug-mode privilege level
resolved_issues.body:
Hi all,
I'm executing some tests after booting Ibex into User-Mode, and asserting debug stimulus, and I see the following:
![Screenshot from 2019-11-12 17-28-49](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16736281/68725023-01090380-0572-11ea-86a8-d11f863ff425.png)
In this test, our debug ROM is located at `0x80004f88`.
We can see that the core's privilege level stays at `PRIV_LVL_U` even after the core has jumped to the debug ROM and `debug_req` has dropped, while the Debug-Mode Spec says that all operation in debug mode should be taken at machine mode. As a result of the current Ibex behavior, illegal instruction exceptions are thrown when we access D-mode CSRs inside of the debug ROM.
However, `dcsr.prv` is being updated properly, and stores the value of `PRIV_LVL_M` after trapping to debug mode, it is just the current privilege mode that is being calculated incorrectly.
Best,
Udi

problem_statement: When Ibex takes a debug request while the core is executing in RISC-V User mode (U-mode), it can jump to the debug ROM while still treating the current execution privilege as U-mode instead of RISC-V Machine mode (M-mode). This affects the debug-entry privilege handling in the core's control and CSR logic. The observed consequence is that code running from the debug ROM can raise illegal-instruction exceptions when it accesses debug control and status registers (CSRs), because those accesses are still being checked as if the core were in U-mode. The expected behavior is that once debug mode is entered, all execution in the debug ROM must run with the core's current privilege level set to M-mode, regardless of the privilege level from which debug was entered.

title: Fix behavior of exceptions in debug mode, document debug CSRs
body:
This PR consists of three small commits which implement the following changes:
- Exceptions in debug mode shall not modify any CSRs. This resolves #168 and is related to #365.
- Document debug CSRs. This resolves #307.
- Update documentation of `mhartid` CSR. Previously, the doc was still describing the cluster and core ID bit fields.

commits.message:
[rtl] Do not update CSRs upon exceptions in debug mode

In debug mode, exceptions shall not update any CSRs including `mcause`,
`mepc`, `mtval`, `dpc` and `mstatus`, see Debug Spec v0.13.2, p.39.

This resolves lowRISC/ibex#168.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

[doc] Document debug CSRs

This resolves lowRISC/ibex#307.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

[doc] Update `mhartid` CSR description

This commit removes outdated bit-field descriptions for `mhartid` CSR.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: Check behavior of exceptions and special instructions related to debug mode
resolved_issues.body:
Currently, exceptions and special instructions are handled independent of whether the core is in debug mode or not. This is not correct for a couple of cases. For example, the Debug Spec v0.13.2 states on p.39 that while in debug mode:
- ~~WFI acts as a NOP. Currently the core just goes to sleep anyway.~~
- Exceptions do not update any registers such as `mcause`, `mepc`, `mtval`, `dpc` and `mstatus`. Currently, exception handling does not depend on debug mode.

~~Similarly, the DRET instruction must lead to an illegal instruction exception when the core is not in debug mode (p.41). Currently, DRET always restores the PC in dpc even if the core is not in debug mode, thus silently messing up the processor state.~~

+.. _csr-dcsr:
+
+Debug Control and Status Register (dcsr)
+----------------------------------------
+
+CSR Address: ``0x7B0``
+
+Reset Value: ``0x4000_0003``
+
+Accessible in Debug Mode only.
+Ibex implements the following bit fields.
+Other bit fields read as zero.
+
++-------+------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
+| Bit#  | R/W  | Description                                                      |
++-------+------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
+| 31:28 | R    | **xdebugver:** 4 = External spec-compliant debug support exists. |
++-------+------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
+| 15    | RW   | **ebreakm:** EBREAK in M-Mode behaves as described in Privileged |
+|       |      | Spec (0), or enters Debug Mode (1).                              |
++-------+------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
+| 12    | WARL | **ebreaku:** EBREAK in U-Mode behaves as described in Privileged |
+|       |      | Spec (0), or enters Debug Mode (1).                              |
++-------+------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
+| 8:6   | R    | **cause:** 1 = EBREAK, 3 = halt request, 4 = step                |
++-------+------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
+| 2     | RW   | **step:** When set and not in Debug Mode, execute a single       |
+|       |      | instruction and enter Debug Mode.                                |
++-------+------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
+| 1:0   | WARL | **prv:** Privilege level the core was operating in when Debug    |
+|       |      | Mode was entered. May be modified by debugger to change          |
+|       |      | privilege level. Ibex allows transitions to all supported modes. |
+|       |      | (M- and U-Mode).                                                 |
++-------+------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
+
+Details of these configuration bits can be found in the RISC-V Debug Specification, version 0.13.2 (see Core Debug Registers, Section 4.8).
+Note that **ebreaku** and **prv** are accidentally specified as RW in version 0.13.2 of the RISC-V Debug Specification.
+More recent versions of the specification define these fields correctly as WARL.
+
+.. _csr-dpc:
+
+Debug PC Register (dpc)
+-----------------------
+
+CSR Address: ``0x7B1``
+
+Reset Value: ``0x0000_0000``
+
+When entering Debug Mode, ``dpc`` is updated with the address of the next instruction that would be executed (if Debug Mode would not have been entered).
+When resuming, the PC is set to the address stored in ``dpc``.
+The debug module may modify ``dpc``.
+Accessible in Debug Mode only.
+
+Debug Scratch Register 0 (dscratch0)
+------------------------------------
+
+CSR Address: ``0x7B2``
+
+Reset Value: ``0x0000_0000``
+
+Scratch register to be used by the debug module.
+Accessible in Debug Mode only.
+
+Debug Scratch Register 1 (dscratch1)
+------------------------------------
+
+CSR Address: ``0x7B3``
+
+Reset Value: ``0x0000_0000``
+
+Scratch register to be used by the debug module.
+Accessible in Debug Mode only.
+

problem_statement: When Ibex takes an exception while the core is already in Debug Mode, the exception-handling path still overwrites machine Control and Status Registers (CSRs) that record trap state. As a result, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, and `mstatus` can be modified even though the core is already in Debug Mode. The affected functionality is the Debug Mode exception/CSR handling logic. The correct behavior is that an exception taken in Debug Mode must leave those CSRs unchanged; in particular, it must not clear the interrupt-enable state in `mstatus` or replace the existing trap information in `mepc`, `mcause`, and `mtval`. This is triggered whenever an exception is taken after `debug_mode` is already active.

problem_statement: `ibex_icache` violates its documented core-side instruction response handshake: `valid_o` can depend on `ready_i`, so the cache may withhold an instruction response that is already available internally until the core raises `ready_i`. The expected behavior is concrete and testable: once the cache has assembled a response for the current fetch, it must assert `valid_o` even while `ready_i` is low; `ready_i` should only control when the core consumes that response. This affects the icache output path back to the core and is exposed when fetch is redirected to a half-word-aligned address. In a design that supports 16-bit compressed instructions, a 32-bit instruction can start on a 16-bit boundary and must then be assembled from two fetch words; that completed 32-bit response must still be presented with `valid_o` independent of `ready_i`.

title: [rtl] prefetch buffer performance fix
body:
- The prefetch buffer needs to know when space is available in the fetch
  FIFO to accept a new external request.
- This change updates that logic to look at what is in the FIFO and what
  is outstanding on the bus to decide when space is available rather
  than always assuming the maximum number of requests are outstanding.
- This improves the usage efficiency of the FIFO and fixes #574

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

resolved_issues.title: Fetch FIFO blocks instruction request when full.
resolved_issues.body:
Hi everyone, 

I may have found an issue with the prefetch buffer. The situation: I have implemented a second memory port in the simple system example (PR #571) and run both the hello_test example and coremark on it. Since I would expect no memory contention on the instruction line, i would expect to record less IFetch waits with coremark. however the opposite was the case: Using the separated data and instruction ports, coremark recoreded around 200 more IFetch wait than using a single memory port.
For the hello_test example, I have found that the new implementation takes two more cycles than the baseline, which already is unexpected. So I have analyzed the situation using this simulation. By comparing the traces of the two hello_test runs, I think I can pinpoint exactly where the problem is:


The top level instruction request signal `instr_req_o` is set in `prefetch_buffer.sv` lines 108-111 by the signal `valid_req`:  
``` 
// Make a new request any time there is space in the FIFO, and space in the request queue
assign valid_new_req = req_i & (fifo_ready | branch_i) & ~rdata_outstanding_q[NUM_REQS-1];
assign valid_req = valid_req_q | valid_new_req;
```
So if we re not branching, a memory request can only be issued when the fifo is ready. The fifo ready signal is set in `ibex_fetch_fifo.sv` line 155:
```
assign in_ready_o = ~valid_q[DEPTH-NUM_REQS]; // DEPTH = 3, NUM_REQS=2
```
Now, by comparing the traces I have found that the delay is introduced around 154ns into the hello_test simulation. The waveform for the baseline implementation is here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47077581/73343178-679fe280-4280-11ea-97b8-4cb615f7b814.png)

The waveform for the implementation with dual port memory is here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47077581/73343091-3e7f5200-4280-11ea-95ef-6e16d835b118.png)


At 143ns you can see that the pipeline is stalled due to the `id_stage` being busy. This is a store-word instruction, so it makes a data request. In the baseline implementation the data and instruction line is shared, so in the meantime no instruction can be fetched. However for the dual-port implementation a new instruction is fetched, and the fetch-fifo after that has stored two memory words. therefore the fifo ready signal will be low, and no new memory request will be made (`instr_req_o`).  
The first instruction (`PC=001003B4`) in the FIFO is compressed. So, after that the word can not be popped and the fifo is still full. Here is content of the fifo at that point (at 149ns):
```
             | 31             16 | 15              0 |
FIFO entry 0 | PC001003B6 [15:0] | PC001003B4 [15:0] |
FIFO entry 1 | PC001003BA [15:0] | PC001003B6 [31:16]| 
```
So instruction `001003B6` is fetched and in the next cycle the fifo is not full anymore. 
```
             | 31             16 | 15              0 |
FIFO entry 0 | PC001003BA [15:0] |                   | 
FIFO entry 0 |                   |                   |
```
So  `instr_req_o` is raised again (at 151ns), but `instr_rvalid_i` is only received in the cycle after that, leading to a 1 cycle stall, since the instruction in the fifo is incomplete.

For the baseline implementation the fifo does not get full and therefore `instr_req_o` is never lowered and we never have to wait for `instr_rvalid_i`. That's the reason why the single-port implementation finishes faster.

So, as far as I can tell, at least while there are unaligned, uncompressed instructions in the fetch fifo, it can never remain full. Thus there is always a stall while waiting for `instr_rvalid_i`. 


I think the fundamental problem is that no simultaneous pop and push is possible while the FIFO is full. If we would take into account the anticipated next-cycle occupancy when setting the fifo `in_ready_o` signal, i. e. change line 155 `ibex_fetch_fifo.sv` to
```
assign in_ready_o = ~valid_d[DEPTH-NUM_REQS]; 
```
the memory request could be done one cycle earlier and the valid signal will arrive only once there is space in the fetch FIFO. 

I have run the hello_test and coremark programs using this fix. The number of IFetch waits for coremark using the fix on the baseline (single-port) implementation decreases from 14968 to 5215. Total ticks decrease from 423620 to 416639.  

Executing the hello_test program, there is no improvement for the single-port implementation. However the additional two cycles of latency that were observed for the dual-port implementation disappear. 

Also coremark now executes with exactly the same statistics for single- and dual-port implementation. This is disapointing, but I think very well possible for non-data intensive workloads. 

I do not know if my fix is fully correct, since there are some parts in the Prefetch Buffer and the Fetch FIFO, that I don't yet completely understand. But I hope that my account may help somebody investigate and fix the problem.

I will attatch the output of my simulation runs. For coremark I will omit the trace_core log and waveforms, since those are huge files. If you are interested in them let me know.

[edit: changed this file, since I have mixed up waveform files. ]
[prefetch-buff-issue_sim-out_new.zip](https://github.com/lowRISC/ibex/files/4127676/prefetch-buff-issue_sim-out_new.zip)




Nomenclature of the folders: master = single-port implementation, perf-eval = dual-port implementation

In perf-eval_hello_test-out, there is a gtkwave save-file `waveconfig.gtkw which you can use with all the simulation waveforms to directly display the waveforms as they are in my screenshots.

cheers, Noam

+    output logic                out_err_o,

 );
 
-  // To gain extra performance DEPTH should be increased, this is due to some inefficiencies in the
-  // way the fetch fifo operates see issue #574 for more details
   localparam int unsigned DEPTH = NUM_REQS+1;
 
   // index 0 is used for output
@@ -159,14 +157,14 @@ module ibex_fetch_fifo #(
   // The LSB of the address is unused, since all addresses are halfword aligned
   assign unused_addr_in = in_addr_i[0];
 
-  ////////////////
-  // input port //
-  ////////////////
+  /////////////////

+  /////////////////
 
-  // Accept data as long as our FIFO has space to accept the maximum number of outstanding
-  // requests. Note that the prefetch buffer does not count how many requests are actually
-  // outstanding, so space must be reserved for the maximum number.
-  assign in_ready_o = ~valid_q[DEPTH-NUM_REQS];
+  // Indicate the fill level of fifo-entries. This is used to determine when a new request can be
+  // made on the bus. The prefetch buffer only needs to know about the upper entries which overlap
+  // with NUM_REQS.

   /////////////////////
   // FIFO management //
diff --git a/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv b/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
index 067867e82e..9343fc0355 100644
--- a/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
+++ b/rtl/ibex_prefetch_buffer.sv
@@ -51,6 +51,7 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_outstanding_n, rdata_outstanding_s, rdata_outstanding_q;
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] branch_discard_n, branch_discard_s, branch_discard_q;
   logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_pmp_err_n, rdata_pmp_err_s, rdata_pmp_err_q;
+  logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] rdata_outstanding_rev;
 
   logic [31:0]         stored_addr_d, stored_addr_q;
   logic                stored_addr_en;
@@ -62,6 +63,7 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (
   logic                fifo_valid;
   logic                fifo_ready;
   logic                fifo_clear;
+  logic [NUM_REQS-1:0] fifo_busy;
 
   ////////////////////////////
   // Prefetch buffer status //
@@ -82,6 +84,16 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (
   // altered the FENCE.I implementation may require changes.
   assign fifo_clear = branch_i;
 
+  // Reversed version of rdata_outstanding_q which can be overlaid with fifo fill state
+  for (genvar i = 0; i < NUM_REQS; i++) begin : gen_rd_rev
+    assign rdata_outstanding_rev[i] = rdata_outstanding_q[NUM_REQS-1-i];
+  end

+  // The fifo is ready to accept a new request if it is not full - including space reserved for
+  // requests already outstanding.
+  // Overlay the fifo fill state with the outstanding requests to see if there is space.
+  assign fifo_ready = ~&(fifo_busy | rdata_outstanding_rev);
+
   ibex_fetch_fifo #(
     .NUM_REQS (NUM_REQS)
   ) fifo_i (
@@ -89,13 +101,12 @@ module ibex_prefetch_buffer (

problem_statement: In the instruction fetch path, the interaction between `ibex_prefetch_buffer` and the fetch FIFO can deassert `instr_req_o` too early when the FIFO is full on a non-branch path and contains a 16-bit compressed instruction followed by a 32-bit instruction that starts in the upper half of one fetched word and completes in the next fetched word. In that state, the next word is requested one cycle late, so after the compressed instruction is consumed the following 32-bit instruction is still incomplete and the core incurs an extra instruction-fetch stall. The expected behavior is that the prefetch buffer must keep requesting the next word needed to complete that spanning 32-bit instruction while the FIFO still holds the compressed instruction and the partial 32-bit instruction, so that once the compressed instruction is consumed the 32-bit instruction is available immediately without an extra fetch bubble.

problem_statement: `fetch_enable_i` is the input that allows the Ibex core to fetch instructions. When the core comes out of reset with `fetch_enable_i` low, the gated core clock can still toggle during the startup idle window instead of staying off. If `fetch_enable_i` is later asserted for only a single cycle, that start request can be missed. The affected reset/startup path is the logic that keeps the core quiescent until fetch is enabled. Correct behavior is that no gated core clock activity should occur while `fetch_enable_i` is low after reset, and even a one-cycle assertion of `fetch_enable_i` must be enough for the core to wake up and issue an instruction fetch request.

title: [rtl] Various security feature bugfixes
body:
- Document that SecureIbex cannot be used without a multiplier and add
  an assertion in the rtl. This fixes #1080.
- Move the PC checking hardware onto its own parameter to match all the
  other individual security features.
- Make the PC increment behavior more sensible on fetch errors (and make
  it match the icache behavior). Factor this into the PC increment check
  to prevent false triggering, fixes #1094.
- Stop the PC mismatch checker firing on dummy instructions, fixes
  #1095.

problem_statement: An instruction bus error in the Ibex instruction-fetch path can be misclassified when it occurs on a 32-bit instruction that starts at a half-word-aligned address, so the instruction spans two 16-bit halves across fetch words. In that case, the fetch logic may treat the faulting instruction as if the first half were a completed 16-bit RISC-V compressed instruction, advance the instruction stream by 2 bytes, and, when SecureIbex's sequential program-counter check is enabled, raise a spurious PC mismatch alarm. The correct behavior is that a fetch error must not cause that unaligned 32-bit instruction to be treated as compressed: the instruction must remain incomplete until both halves are available, and the next sequential PC tracked by the fetch path must advance by 4 bytes rather than 2. This affects the instruction fetch FIFO/front-end and is triggered by a sequential instruction bus error during an unaligned 32-bit instruction fetch.

title: [rtl] Fix performance counter bug
body:

resolved_issues.title: Illegal Instruction Retires
resolved_issues.body:
####  RISC-V Specification

> 3.1.11: "The minstret CSR counts the number of instructions the hart has retired. The mcycle and minstret registers
have 64-bit precision on all RV32 and RV64 systems.

> The counter registers have an arbitrary value after system reset, and can be written with a given value. Any CSR write takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed."

> The counter-inhibit register mcountinhibit is a 32-bit WARL register that controls which of the hardware performance-monitoring counters increment. The settings in this register only control whether the counters increment; their accessibility is not affected by the setting of this register.

> When the CY, IR, or HPMn bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the cycle, instret, or hpmcountern register increments as usual. When the CY, IR, or HPMn bit is set, the corresponding counter does not increment.

####  Issue Description
An illegal instruction increments the minstret counter as if it was a legal one.

#### Steps to Reproduce

As shown below, the minstret counter is incremented for the illegal instruction csrrw x8, 0x010, x3, knowing that IR bit of mcountinhibit is set to '0 and thus allowing for the minstret to be incremented.  

![minstret_ill](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/54367010/95972699-0e2e1280-0e13-11eb-87f8-9621c1352d6b.PNG)

---
Product: OneSpin 360 DV-Verify
App: Processor Verification App
Tool's version: 2020.2.0

problem_statement: The Ibex instruction-retirement counter path can count a trapping instruction as if it had retired normally. With retired-instruction counting enabled (`mcountinhibit.IR = 0`), `minstret` is observed to increment for an illegal instruction, and the same bug appears for `ECALL` (the RISC-V environment-call instruction): if software reads `minstret`, executes `ECALL`, and the trap handler reads `minstret` on entry, the second value should be exactly one count higher because only the earlier read instruction retired, but the trapping `ECALL` is currently counted as well. The affected logic is the instruction-retirement/performance-counter path between the core pipeline and the CSR counter block. The correct behavior is that `minstret` increments only for instructions that complete and retire normally; instructions that raise a synchronous exception, including illegal instructions and `ECALL`, must not contribute to the retired-instruction count.

`INSTR_BALL` was introduced in 47b713fd as a vector instruction.
This is not used and is probably a leftover so can be removed.

definitions to decode the instructions.

latch.

Remove those occurrences.

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/ibex || exit 1

export PATH="/opt/micromamba/envs/ibex/bin:/opt/micromamba/condabin:$PATH"
export USER_CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/micromamba/envs/ibex/include"
export USER_LDFLAGS="-L/opt/micromamba/envs/ibex/lib"

set -uo pipefail
set +e

TEST_BUILD="simple_system_verilator_build"
TEST_TRACER="tracer_unused_without_suppression"
TB_DIR="/home/ibex/.tb_pr1229_verilator_warnings"
BUILD_LOG="${TB_DIR}/simple_system_build.log"
TRACER_LOG="${TB_DIR}/tracer_lint.log"

rm -rf "${TB_DIR}" build
mkdir -p "${TB_DIR}"

timeout 1200s fusesoc --cores-root=. run --target=sim --setup --build \
  lowrisc:ibex:ibex_simple_system > "${BUILD_LOG}" 2>&1
build_rc=$?

cat > "${TB_DIR}/ibex_pkg_unused_only.vlt" <<'EOF'
`verilator_config
lint_off -rule UNUSED -file "*rtl/ibex_pkg.sv"
EOF

verilator -E -P -sv rtl/ibex_tracer_pkg.sv | \
  sed '/verilator[[:space:]]\+lint_/d' > "${TB_DIR}/ibex_tracer_pkg_stripped.sv"
pp_pkg_rc=$?
verilator -E -P -sv rtl/ibex_tracer.sv | \
  sed '/verilator[[:space:]]\+lint_/d' > "${TB_DIR}/ibex_tracer_stripped.sv"
pp_tracer_rc=$?

if [ "${pp_pkg_rc}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${pp_tracer_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  timeout 300s verilator --lint-only -Wall -Werror-UNUSED -Wno-DECLFILENAME \
    --top-module ibex_tracer \
    "${TB_DIR}/ibex_pkg_unused_only.vlt" \
    rtl/ibex_pkg.sv \
    "${TB_DIR}/ibex_tracer_pkg_stripped.sv" \
    "${TB_DIR}/ibex_tracer_stripped.sv" \
    > "${TRACER_LOG}" 2>&1
  tracer_rc=$?
else
  tracer_rc=1
  {
    echo "Failed to preprocess tracer sources."
    echo "ibex_tracer_pkg.sv rc=${pp_pkg_rc}"
    echo "ibex_tracer.sv rc=${pp_tracer_rc}"
  } > "${TRACER_LOG}"
fi

if [ "${build_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
  cat "${BUILD_LOG}"
fi

if [ "${tracer_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
  cat "${TRACER_LOG}"
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "${build_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_BUILD} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_BUILD} ... FAIL"
fi

if [ "${tracer_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_TRACER} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_TRACER} ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

if [ "${build_rc}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${tracer_rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

exit 1

problem_statement: Building the `lowrisc:ibex:ibex_simple_system` Verilator simulation fails on recent Verilator versions because warnings are treated as fatal. In the baseline, the build emits `UNUSED` warnings from `rtl/ibex_tracer_pkg.sv` and `LATCH` warnings from `shared/rtl/bus.sv`, then exits with an error instead of completing. The affected functionality is the `ibex_simple_system` Verilator build, specifically the tracer package and shared bus logic compiled for that target. The expected behavior is that this build completes successfully on those Verilator versions without fatal unused-parameter or inferred-latch warnings from those sources.

title: Various fixes for known simulation issues
body: Small fixes to the RTL and testbench to fix issues seen in nightly runs

repo.name: ibex
repo.description: Ibex is a small 32 bit RISC-V CPU core, previously known as zero-riscy.

commits.message:
[rtl] Add reset to lockstep delayed inputs

In tests with multiple resets, these signals could hold onto spurious
values through reset (since the clock is also gated) which caused
assertion failures on resumption.

Fixes #1368

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

[rtl] Fix decode values for B Operand mux select

With data-independent timing enabled and BranchTargetALU configured,
branches will stall for a cycle causing an illegal value to be decoded
for the B Operand. No functional impact of this, but an assertion fires
so we might as well tie it off properly.

Fixes #1367

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

[dv/uvm/core_ibex] Update CSR description file

The CSR tests don't currently support multiple configurations
(see #1333). Since the OpenTitan configuration is the only one currently
being run, update this file to pass with that for now.

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>

[dv/uvm/core_ibex] Pass ISA from Makefile

This allows run.py to pass ISA options through to Spike. This relates to
the failure in #1369 (test inserts a bitmanip instruction which Spike
interprets as valid but the core treats as invalid depending on config).

Signed-off-by: Tom Roberts <tomroberts@lowrisc.org>
